title: Hardcoded event reference 'E1' in demo review fixtures introduces unverified data dependency
evidence: In scripts/demo_reviews.py fixture(), each generated row hardcodes 'E1' for evidence_refs across all 24 cases. However, scripts/verify_packet.py validate_case() allows any event identifier matching regex r'E[1-9]\d*'; it does not require an event named 'E1' to exist. If a structurally valid synthetic case in data/cases.json defines events starting at 'E2' or 'E10', PacketVerifier.verify() passes, but scripts.demo_reviews fails with ValueError: 'unknown evidence reference' during ReviewStudy.load_submission().
suggested_fix: Dynamically select a known valid event identifier from the loaded case instead of hardcoding 'E1', e.g.: study.cases[case_id]['events'][0]['id'].
resolution_reason: Corrected dynamic event references after a valid non-E1 packet and failing integration regression reproduced the defect.

title: Symlink loop resolution in resolve_path catches RuntimeError but omits OSError
evidence: On POSIX platforms under Python 3.11, resolving a recursive symlink via Path.resolve() can raise OSError (specifically Errno 40: ELOOP 'Too many levels of symbolic links') rather than RuntimeError. When called directly as a Python library API (outside the CLI main() handlers, which broadly catch OSError), resolve_path() leaks OSError rather than normalizing it to ValueError('invalid filesystem path') as intended by BUG-008.
suggested_fix: Change the exception handler in resolve_path() to catch both: except (RuntimeError, OSError):
resolution_reason: No documented library promise normalizes every OSError to ValueError. Python 3.11 self-loop raised normalized ValueError; 3.14 nonstrict resolution returned and intake rejected it safely. Existing CLI test passes both versions. No reproduced CLI leak.

title: Test test_unknown_category_is_counted_as_a_real_label is misnamed and does not exercise the unknown category
description:
def test_unknown_category_is_counted_as_a_real_label(self):
    result = review_tools.agreement(CATEGORIES, list(reversed(CATEGORIES)), CATEGORIES)
    self.assertEqual(result["count"], 3)
    self.assertEqual(result["agree"], 1)
    self.assertAlmostEqual(result["kappa"], 0)
evidence: CATEGORIES in tests/test_reviews.py is defined as ['review_needed', 'no_supported_defect', 'insufficient_evidence']. None of these values is 'unknown'. The test actually exercises zero-kappa inverted symmetric off-diagonal ratings. The category 'unknown' exists in DIMENSIONS['outcome'], DIMENSIONS['decision'], and DIMENSIONS['procedure'], but is not tested here.
suggested_fix: Rename test_unknown_category_is_counted_as_a_real_label to test_inverted_symmetric_ratings_yield_zero_kappa and add an explicit test verifying agreement calculations over domains containing 'unknown' values.
resolution_reason: Renamed the test to insufficient_evidence and asserted both category marginals. No duplicate test appended.

title: Non-atomic demo directory creation leaves unmanaged partial state on interrupted runs
evidence: build_demo() calls output.mkdir() before generating files. If process termination, SIGINT, or an unexpected I/O failure occurs before demo_manifest.json is written, the output directory remains on disk partially populated. Because build_demo() enforces require(not output.exists(), 'demo destination already exists'), rerun attempts fail immediately until manual filesystem cleanup is performed.
suggested_fix: Generate fixture files in a temporary staging directory and atomically move/rename to the final destination upon successful completion, or add cleanup exception handling.
resolution_reason: Atomic output publication was not promised. Interrupted partial output is a retained limitation; documented completion/retry rules and GAP-003 track a possible enhancement. No automatic deletion or overwrite introduced.

title: Independence-claim regression test passes even if case_author and prior_exposure are ignored
description: The right submission is built with fixture(name="rater_b", kind="human") and default metadata: independence_attested=False, prior_exposure="unknown". Either value alone makes compare() return REQUIRES_INDEPENDENCE_REVIEW, whatever the left submission claims. The left-side case_author=True and author_expectations_seen inputs are never what triggers the expected result. No other test covers a case author or exposed reviewer paired with a fully attested independent reviewer.
evidence: Mutation: replace the elif condition with `any(not m["independence_attested"] for m in metadata)`. The test still passes. Yet two human submissions with independence_attested=True, prior_exposure="none_declared" and case_author=True would then report DECLARED_ONLY instead of REQUIRES_INDEPENDENCE_REVIEW.
suggested_fix: Give the right submission metadata={"independence_attested": True, "prior_exposure": "none_declared"} so that only the left claim varies. Add a symmetric case where the claim is on the right.
resolution_reason: A source mutant ignoring author/exposure survived original tests. Strengthened test isolates each flag against a fully attested opposite reviewer on both sides; mutant is now rejected.

title: Nonfinite-JSON test is vacuous, and nonfinite rejection misses overflowing float literals
description: The test writes the manifest '{"case_count": NaN}'. If NaN were accepted, verify_manifest would still raise ValueError at `set(manifest) == self.MANIFEST_FIELDS`, so the test cannot detect removal of parse_constant. Separately, parse_json overrides only parse_constant (NaN/Infinity/-Infinity). json.loads parses '1e999' through float() to inf, so a nonfinite value is accepted. Current impact is nil: no numeric field is consumed except case_count, which requires type int. The BUG-003 and TESTING.md claim that nonfinite JSON is rejected is broader than the implementation.
evidence: Mutation: delete `parse_constant=cls.reject_constant`; the test still passes. Counterexample: PacketVerifier.parse_json(b'{"x": 1e999}') returns {'x': inf} with no error.
suggested_fix: Add a parse_float hook that rejects non-finite results (e.g. `lambda s: require_finite(float(s))`). Rewrite the test on a full manifest copy with only one value replaced by NaN, and separately by 1e999, so that only the nonfinite check can fail.
resolution_reason: Replaced vacuous manifest-shape test with direct parser contracts and finite-value acceptance. Overflow reproduction failed before adding finite parse_float handling.

title: CSV row-width checks are not discriminated by tests; intake width check has no regression at all
description: The template test appends the non-empty cell ',hidden_answer'. With csv.reader, the blank check `all(value == "" for value in row[1:])` already rejects it, so removing the width check does not fail the test. A surplus empty cell (trailing ',') is caught only by the width check and is untested. In load_submission, `dict(zip(FIELDS, values))` silently truncates surplus cells if the width check is removed. Short rows raise KeyError rather than ValueError. No test supplies a completed submission with wrong row width.
evidence: Mutation A: drop `all(len(row) == len(FIELDS) for row in data)` in verify_reviewer; test_rejects_extra_csv_cells still passes. Mutation B: drop the width clause in load_submission; every test still passes, and a completed CSV whose row 1 ends with ',secret' is accepted with the extra cell discarded.
suggested_fix: Change the template test to append an empty cell (',') and relock. Add intake tests for a surplus empty cell, a surplus non-empty cell and a short row, each expecting ValueError.
resolution_reason: Template width test now appends an empty surplus cell. Completed intake has explicit empty/nonempty surplus and short-row regressions; existing guard retained.

title: Reviewer README.md and A/B separation are unvalidated despite 'label-contaminated' rejection claim
description: verify_reviewer checks the reviewer file-name set, parsed cases (compared as a dict keyed by id, so order-insensitive), rubric bytes and blank labels. README.md is only hash-locked, with no content constraint and no A/B consistency check. Nothing checks that A and B differ in ordering, or that reviewer_packets/A is not a symlink to reviewer_packets/B. path() only requires resolution inside the packet root, not inside the reviewer folder. Hashes protect against later drift, but anyone who regenerates the manifest can embed expectations in a README and still get STRUCTURE_VERIFIED.
location: scripts/verify_packet.py::PacketVerifier.verify_reviewer and REVIEWER_FILES; documentation/TESTING.md ('reject ... label-contaminated'); README.md deliverable 3 ('separately ordered')
evidence: In a packet copy, add the line 'SL03 expected: review_needed' to reviewer_packets/A/README.md and update its manifest digest; verify() returns STRUCTURE_VERIFIED. Alternatively, replace reviewer_packets/B with a symlink to A and relock; verification passes with identical ordering.
suggested_fix: Require each reviewer README to match a canonical template, or A==B byte equality minus a declared ordering note. Reject symlinked reviewer directories and files, or require them to resolve inside their own reviewer folder. If separate ordering is a study property, assert that A and B case orders differ. Otherwise narrow the TESTING.md claim to 'structured fields and labels.csv'.
resolution_reason: Narrowed testing claims to structural labels/forms and documented free-text/order inspection as procedural. Relocking a modified packet is not an authenticity attack the tool claims to prevent; no canonical-README or isolation guarantee added.

title: Normative review protocol and intake semantics are not bound to the locked packet or the report
description: The locked rubric tells reviewers that completed submissions need the sidecar 'described in the review protocol'. docs/review_protocol.md is neither in locked_paths nor in REVIEWER_FILES, so a reviewer holding only their directory cannot read it, and edits do not change packet identity. Allowed dimension values, reason codes and the 20/0.70 gate are hard-coded in review_tools.py, which duplicates the rubric. No test asserts the two stay consistent, and reports carry no tool version or source digest. They currently match on static comparison.
location: scripts/verify_packet.py::PacketVerifier.locked_paths; docs/rubric.md ('metadata sidecar described in the review protocol'); scripts/review_tools.py::DIMENSIONS, REASONS, ReviewStudy.compare
evidence: Edit docs/review_protocol.md, or add a reason code to REASONS without a rubric change. Packet verification and the manifest/rubric digests in existing submission metadata still match, and reports are indistinguishable from pre-change reports.
suggested_fix: Lock docs/review_protocol.md, or move the sidecar instructions into a locked reviewer file. Add a test that parses the rubric table and reason lists and compares them to DIMENSIONS and REASONS. Include a tool/contract version, or a digest of review_tools.py, in the agreement report.
resolution_reason: Added tool_version to reports. Freezing/distributing normative instructions and centralizing rubric constants are before-M2 work in GAP-004; this ops guide/source is not presently manifest-locked. No human collection or acceptance claimed.

title: Regex `\d` accepts non-ASCII digits in elapsed_seconds and identifiers
description: Python str patterns match Unicode decimal digits with \d by default. The rubric requires elapsed_seconds to be a nonnegative integer and implies ASCII identifiers.
evidence: elapsed_seconds='1\u0660' (ARABIC-INDIC DIGIT ZERO) matches `0|[1-9]\d*` and is accepted. validate_case accepts id 'SL\u0660\u0661' and event id 'E1\u0663'. Visually confusable IDs could then be cited.
suggested_fix: Use [0-9] or compile with re.ASCII. Optionally bound elapsed_seconds to a plausible maximum.
resolution_reason: Identifiers and elapsed digits now explicitly use ASCII ranges, protected by failure tests.

title: Excel-style UTF-8 BOM returns are rejected with an undiagnosable error
description: A completed CSV saved as 'CSV UTF-8' by common spreadsheet tools begins with a BOM. decode('utf-8') keeps U+FEFF, so table[0][0] == '\ufeffcase_id' and the header check fails. The CLI emits only {"status":"ERROR","reason":"ValueError"}, discarding the constant, non-sensitive require() message. The protocol asks coordinators to preserve original submissions, so the only remedy is editing a copy without knowing which check failed.
evidence: Prefix a valid fixture CSV with b'\xef\xbb\xbf' and recompute responses_sha256. load_submission raises ValueError('invalid CSV header'), and the CLI shows only 'ValueError'.
suggested_fix: Either decode with 'utf-8-sig' (the digest is still over the raw bytes) or reject BOMs explicitly with a documented code. Raise a dedicated ValidationError from require() and print its constant message, while keeping type-only output for other exceptions.
resolution_reason: UTF-8 BOM accepted at parsing without altering raw hashed bytes; regression covers immutable originals. Type-only CLI diagnostics remain an explicit privacy trade-off.

title: Snapshot regression tests compare resolved roots to unresolved temp paths and fail on symlinked temp dirs
description: PacketVerifier.root is resolve_path(root), but csv_path.parent and packet come from tempfile without resolution. Where the temp directory is behind a symlink (e.g. macOS /var -> /private/var), the injected concurrent edit never fires. The first test then fails `len(reads) == 1`, and the second fails assertRaises on re-verify. They fail rather than pass vacuously, but the BUG-006/BUG-007 evidence is platform-dependent.
evidence: Run with TMPDIR pointing at a symlinked directory. The comparison is False, so no edit happens and both tests fail.
suggested_fix: Compare against Path(...).resolve() in the patched hooks, or resolve self.folder in setUp.
resolution_reason: Original snapshot tests fail with symlinked TMPDIR; resolved test fixtures pass in that environment.

title: Path-boundary check and open are not atomic (symlink swap / FIFO races)
description: path() resolves `self.root / relative` and checks is_relative_to, then read_bytes calls is_file() and opens the unresolved path. A concurrent writer can replace a component with a symlink after the check, so the bounded read leaves the root. It can also substitute a FIFO after is_file(), so open/read blocks. architecture.md states that shared bounded reads 'enforce path boundaries'. The README disclaims filesystem isolation for blinding, not for read confinement.
evidence: Race: between resolve_path(path).is_relative_to(self.root) and path.open('rb'), rename review_returns/a.csv to a symlink to /etc/hostname (or mkfifo in its place). The read follows the new target, or hangs.
suggested_fix: Open first, then validate: os.open with O_NOFOLLOW (and O_NONBLOCK), fstat for S_ISREG, and compare the opened file's realpath or device/inode with the checked one. Alternatively, document the non-concurrent-writer assumption explicitly.
resolution_reason: Active hostile filesystem writers are outside current local-file threat model. Explicit stable-owned-directory requirement and separate-open race are documented; GAP-005 blocks treating it as hosted untrusted intake.

title: ReviewSubmission is documented as 'validated' but direct construction bypasses validation; compare() revalidation is partial
description: compare() revalidates row values and study hashes but not metadata fields, nor that each rows key equals row['case_id']. architecture.md and issues.md explicitly call direct construction a trusted interface, so this is not a defect. The class docstring overstates it.
evidence: ReviewSubmission(meta_forged_human_independent, {'SL01': row_for_SL02, 'SL02': row_for_SL01, ...}) passes compare() with misaligned labels and DECLARED_ONLY eligibility.
suggested_fix: Reword the docstring. Optionally assert key == row['case_id'] and re-run the non-digest parts of validate_metadata in compare(), which costs little.
resolution_reason: Value-object docstring corrected to identify load_submission as the validation boundary. Trusted direct construction remains explicitly unsupported as authentication.

title: Contract-required control-case and prevalence-sensitivity reporting is not implemented
description: Reports contain per-dimension matrices, marginals, kappa and Wilson intervals. They have no control-subset breakdown, since author designations are deliberately excluded from the public packet, and no prevalence-adjusted statistic. human_gate is hard-coded PENDING and the limitations text mentions control cases, so nothing is overclaimed. A complete gate report would need extra tooling.
location: docs/evaluation_contract.md ('Report separate agreement ... on author-designated justified-denial controls'; 'Discuss prevalence sensitivity'); scripts/review_tools.py::ReviewStudy.compare
suggested_fix: Before human data exists, define how control designations will be supplied after locking, and which prevalence diagnostics (e.g. PABAK, per-category agreement) will be reported.
resolution_reason: Control subsets and prevalence interpretation remain manual before-M2 gates. No study acceptance is emitted; no automatic adjustment statistic added without a preregistered interpretation.

title: collected_at accepts implausible declared times
description: Only a timezone-aware ISO datetime is required. A collection time before the packet existed (created_on 2026-11-08), or far in the future, is accepted. Metadata are documented as declarations, so this is a plausibility gap, not an authentication defect.
suggested_fix: Optionally require collected_at >= the packet creation date and flag future times in the report as a provenance warning.
resolution_reason: Collection time is a self-declaration checked for format/timezone, not temporal authenticity. Manual provenance review remains required; no automatic human pass is possible.

title: Minor documentation inconsistencies
description: AGENTS.md lists verify_packet, unittest and flake8 as the final gate. TESTING.md adds bandit and pip_audit. issues.md describes five bugs as 'four defect groups' plus BUG-005 without stating the grouping. Neither affects runtime behavior.
location: AGENTS.md (final gate list) vs documentation/TESTING.md (gate list); issues.md ('four defect groups' vs BUG-001..005)
suggested_fix: Align the gate lists and state the grouping explicitly.
resolution_reason: Agent final-gate text aligned with TESTING.md; historical four initial groups plus later fifth correction clarified.
